summary: Norway's Equinor is still cleaning up after a real cyberattack on its office IT systems, and production is not affected. The NSA's internal network is reportedly back up, but staff are still arriving in staggered shifts. The White House says it sees no sign of a coordinated attack.

events.title: Norway's Equinor still cleaning up after cyberattack on IT systems
events.impact: Equinor says oil and gas production is unaffected and it sees no sign of stolen data. One employee told media the internal email was down. No time estimate for full recovery.
events.stated_cause: Equinor calls it a cyberattack but not a virus, so it says it will not spread. On Nov 18 it said it better understands how it happened. Who did it is unknown. Norway's security agency NSM is assisting.

events.title: NSA classified internal network (NSANet) reportedly back up, staggered staffing continues
events.impact: CBS cites two sources saying NSANet is running again. Staff still arrive in shifts for fear the network cannot handle everyone at once. NSA says mission-critical sharing was not hurt. No end date for the shifts.
events.stated_cause: The Director of National Intelligence linked it to urgent patching of PHP software flaws that kept some systems from restarting. The NSA first said routine maintenance. No official source reports a cyber attack.

events.title: FAA nationwide ground stop; Juniper router installs paused
events.impact: Flights have resumed. The FAA paused new Juniper router installs and disabled one function on 60+ other routers. Senators want answers on testing. FAA feed at 04:04 UTC shows only a wind delay at SFO.
events.stated_cause: The FAA says one new router at a site in El Dorado, Arkansas flooded the network with data. It does not know what triggered it. HPE says its gear worked as configured. The FBI is helping to rule out an attack.

events.title: US stocks mixed Nov 18; Dow down 1.1%, Nasdaq up 0.4%
events.impact: Nov 18 close: Dow fell 561 points to about 50,198, S&P 500 fell 0.2% to about 7,323, Nasdaq rose 0.4% to about 24,429. I saw no trading halts or exchange problems.
events.stated_cause: Reports point to Nvidia results, worry about AI stocks, and hawkish Fed minutes that signal possible rate hikes. No technical or attack cause reported.

events.title: Bitcoin about 62.5K to 64.8K USD, down roughly 12-15% on the week
events.impact: Coinbase shows about 63,987 and CoinGecko about 62,521. Crypto.com shows about 64,310. It is a slow slide, not a crash. I found no exchange outage.
events.stated_cause: Market notes point to Fed rate-hike worries and a weak risk mood. No technical or attack cause reported.

events.title: White House says no sign of coordinated cyberattack behind recent outages
events.impact: Officials call the outages separate maintenance and technical problems. The Homeland Security Secretary earlier said he was not ruling out anything. Some outlets report public doubt about the timing.
events.stated_cause: Officials cite patching, router work and software bugs, not an attacker. This is an official view, not a proven finding.

events.title: Apple services (iCloud, App Store) outage
events.impact: Thousands of users reported problems. Apple says services are back up.
events.stated_cause: Apple says an internal update caused it and told media it was not a cyberattack.

events.title: Chase banking services disrupted
events.impact: Some Chase customers could not use certain services on Monday. Chase looks operational now.
events.stated_cause: Chase says a software bug in an on-site hardware system caused it, and it is not cyber-related.

events.title: Cloudflare status page shows degraded performance
events.impact: The status page lists degraded performance for some services, last changed about 03:19 UTC today. I saw no wire report of a wide outage.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. Cloudflare has not given a cause in the data I saw.

events.title: CISA adds four actively exploited flaws to its list
events.impact: Routine notice covering Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap software. I saw no new Emergency Directive. The notice does not mention the outages.
events.stated_cause: Attackers are exploiting software flaws. CISA gives no link to the outages.

connection_assessment.reasoning: The NSA says patching, the FAA points to one new router, Apple and Chase name internal software problems, and Equinor reports a real attack with no named culprit. Officials say these are separate, but the White House cannot fully rule things out. No official source ties Equinor to the US outages.
connection_assessment.would_change_my_mind: An official statement blaming one company or attacker for several of these, or more big systems failing at the same moment.

alert.reason: No new confirmed link between incidents and no widespread new failure in the last few hours.

prep_note: No action needed for most people. Keep some cash and your phone charged, as you would for any outage. Update your devices and apps when patches arrive. If you run a business, check that your own software updates are tested before rollout.
